item.title: Sexual violence: UK, Mirabel Centre push for stronger protection, justice for survivors
item.description: By Henry Ojelu The United Kingdom and the Mirabel Centre have renewed calls for stronger protection, sustained support and access to justice for survivors of sexual and gender-based violence in Nigeria. The British Deputy High Commissioner in Lagos, Mr Jonny Baxter, and founder of the Mirabel Centre, Itoro Eze-Anaba, made the call on Thursday at a special reception and panel discussion in Lagos to mark the centre’s milestone of supporting more than 10,000 survivors of sexual violence. The event, held as part of the 2026 16 Days of Activism Against Gender-Based Violence, also featured the launch of the centre’s landmark publication, The Survivor Experience: A Voice That Matters. Speaking on the theme, “A Milestone of Care, A Call for Sustained Support & Justice,” Baxter said although the achievement deserved celebration, sexual violence remained a difficult issue requiring sustained attention and commitment. He said: “We want to celebrate 10,000 survivors, but we also want to ensure that many more people are able to access the professional support and services they need.” The British envoy stressed the importance of placing survivors’ experiences at the centre of interventions, noting that their voices were essential to understanding the challenges they faced and improving access to support and justice. He said the UK remained committed to ending violence against women and girls in all its forms through development partnerships, programmes and collaboration with governments and civil society organisations. Baxter disclosed that the UK would soon host an international summit focusing on technology-facilitated gender-based violence, noting that emerging forms of abuse required new approaches, tools and solutions. He also commended the Mirabel Centre for its pioneering work, describing it as a Nigerian organisation addressing local challenges and changing lives through its support for survivors. Earlier, Eze-Anaba said the centre’s journey could not be told without acknowledging the contributions of the British Council, the Department for International Development and the British High Commission. She disclosed that the British High Commission provided funding for the centre’s first three years and continued to support its work through partnerships and opportunities to advocate for survivors. According to her, the achievement was not merely about the number of survivors supported but the quality, dignity and respect with which services were delivered. “Today is not about public relations for the Mirabel Centre. It is about the services we provide and how those services are shared in a dignified manner for survivors,” she said. Eze-Anaba said the centre regularly sought feedback from survivors to assess its services and identify areas requiring improvement. item.title: ‘We wished you stayed longer’ – Nkem Owoh mourns Pete Edochie
item.description: Veteran Nollywood actor Nkem Owoh has paid tribute to his late colleague and friend, Pete Edochie, expressing regret that the legendary actor did not live long enough to celebrate his 80th birthday. Owoh, in a tribute shared on his Instagram page, described Edochie as a dear brother and friend who made people believe in humanity through the way he lived and treated those around him. The actor recalled that Edochie had celebrated his 70th birthday in a special way, during which he spoke about their shared experience in the movie Ikuku . Owoh said he had looked forward to sharing his own story about Edochie when the latter turned 80 on March 7, 2027. However, he lamented that death had taken his friend before the milestone birthday. “I was waiting to tell my own story about you on your 80th birthday, which is on 7th March, 2027. But death had another plan. Who are we to question God?” he wrote. The actor added that he and others had wished Edochie could live a little longer to witness the celebration they had anticipated. “We would have wished you stayed a bit longer to see that great day we were all looking forward to,” he said. Describing the late actor with his traditional titles, including Ogadagidi, Ebubedike and Ononenyi na Nteje, Owoh said Edochie had lived a fulfilled life and prayed for blessings upon his family. “You lived well and we are assured of your place in heaven. Rest well, my friend and brother. May your passing bring immeasurable blessings to your family,” he wrote. He concluded his tribute by describing Edochie as an irreplaceable legend and bidding him farewell with the words, “Ijeoma, Ebube Dike Ndi Igbo.” The post ‘We wished you stayed longer’ – Nkem Owoh mourns Pete Edochie appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Ojukwu Memorial: Bianca slams South East governors over disunity, rivalries
item.description: . Laments abandonment of Ojukwu by political elite he helped make . Urges Igbo youths in diaspora to shun illicit wealth . As Uwazurike demands Nnamdi Kanu’s release . Insists Biafra struggle must be non-violent By Steve Oko UMUAHIA — Nigeria’s Minister of Foreign Affairs, Ambassador Bianca Ojukwu, has berated Igbo political leaders, particularly governors in the South-East, for failing to unite in the interest of the people, lamenting that their mutual antagonism was undermining the region’s collective progress. This is as the Founder of the Movement for the Actualisation of the Sovereign State of Biafra (MASSOB BIM), Chief Ralph Uwazurike, has renewed his call for the release of the detained Biafra agitator, Mazi Nnamdi Kanu, insisting that he committed no offence warranting his continued detention. Bianca, widow of the late Biafran leader, Chukwuemeka Odumegwu-Ojukwu, said the governors had failed to speak with one voice on issues affecting the Igbo, choosing instead to antagonise one another at the expense of the people. She spoke on Thursday at the 15th annual memorial of the late Igbo leader held at the Ojukwu Memorial Library, Owerri, where she called for a departure from political rivalry, personal interests and divisive tendencies. Expressing disappointment with the state of Igbo unity, she said the region could not continue to demand recognition from others while its leaders and people failed to recognise and value one another. “We cannot continue to celebrate Igbo greatness while tolerating the disunity that undermines it,” she declared. The minister lamented that Igbo governors were not sufficiently united to advance the interests of their people, insisting that unity must transcend rhetoric and cultural gatherings to become a practical commitment to regional development. She urged the governors to collaborate for the common good, stressing that the future of the South-East could not be built on mutual suspicion, political antagonism and personal ambition. Bianca also expressed disappointment with some Igbo political elites who, despite benefiting from the influence and political legacy of her late husband, had abandoned him and failed to sustain the ideals he stood for. She said Ojukwu’s legacy should not be reduced to the celebration of his military exploits, titles, speeches and political struggles, but should be understood through his convictions, humanity and commitment to justice and dignity. The minister said her late husband was a soldier, statesman, intellectual and patriarch whose life was driven by a profound belief in justice and the right of people to live without fear. Reflecting on the painful history of the Igbo, particularly the 1966 pogroms, displacement and civil war, she said remembrance of Ojukwu should serve as a commitment to preventing a recurrence of such tragedies rather than merely celebrating the circumstances that made him famous. item.title: Super Falcons: Eguavon invites 24 players for Algeria friendlies
item.description: By Enitan Abdultawab Nigeria’s Super Falcons have named a 24 player squad for their upcoming international friendlies against Algeria, with goalkeeper Chiamaka Nnadozie and forward Asisat Oshoala among the key players selected. The squad, announced by interim coach Augustine Eguavoen, will face Algeria on November 30 in Algiers before meeting the North African side again on December 4 in Tizi-Ouzou. Captain Rasheedat Ajibade is, however, absent from the list as she continues her recovery from surgery. The two matches are expected to provide the Falcons with an opportunity to prepare for their Olympic qualifying encounter against Morocco scheduled for March 2027. Nnadozie, Comfort Erhabor and Christiana Uzoma are the three goalkeepers selected for the fixtures. The defensive department comprises Michelle Alozie, Shukurat Oladipo, Glory Ogbonna, Oluwatosin Demehin, Glory Edet, Valentina Uroko and Nicole Payne. In midfield, Eguavoen has called up Christy Ucheibe, Joy Igbokwe, Regina Otu, Fatimoh Solaty, Suliat Abideen, Toni Payne and Jennifer Echegini. Oshoala will lead the attacking options alongside Folashade Ijamilusi, Shakirat Moshood, Blessing Okpe, Joy Omewa, Blessing Nkor and Olamide Adugbe. The friendlies form part of Nigeria’s preparations as the team looks to secure qualification for the 2028 Olympic Games. item.title: NDC using ‘rig and die’ slogan to mobilise for mass rigging – Keyamo
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: The Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo SAN, has accused the Nigeria Democratic Congress NDC of using the “rig and die” slogan as a cover to mobilise its members and “rig the elections massively.” Keyamo made the claim on Thursday in a post on his X account. He was reacting to a clarification of the slogan by the NDC presidential candidate, Peter Obi. “There is no need for Peter Obi to clarify the ‘rig and die’ slogan and do damage control. We know what it means. The slogan is nothing but a subterfuge for them to mobilise themselves and rig the elections massively as they did in a part of the country in 2023 but still failed”, he said. The minister asked what would stop a party that is “sufficiently armed to play the role of law-enforcement agents” from rigging elections itself. “If a party in a contest with other parties is sufficiently armed to play the role of law-enforcement agents, what stops that same party from rigging the elections itself? Are they saints?” he asked. He argued that no party can be both contestant and referee. “You cannot be a participant in a contest, yet you want to act as the umpire under the guise that you don’t trust the umpire! That is creating a graver absurdity than the one you’re trying to solve!” he said. The slogan became a national talking point after a former Deputy Senate President, Ovie Omo-Agege, the NDC candidate for Delta Central Senatorial District, used it at a campaign event in Uvwie, Delta State, in October. “Anybody who rigs the election on that day, we will kill him!” Omo-Agege said, adding: “It is rig and die.” Tension over the slogan grew after gunmen attacked Omo-Agege’s campaign team at Uduere, in Ughelli North Local Government Area of Delta State, this Monday. His media adviser, Sunny Areh, said four people were killed and four others critically injured, while Omo-Agege was unhurt. Other reports put the death toll at six. Keyamo condemned the killings the same day. He asked promoters of the slogan to “publicly withdraw it, and apologise for overheating the political temperature.” “It is wrong to tell your supporters to kill other citizens under whatever guise. It smacks of desperation,” he said then. Obi and his running mate, Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso, later visited the families of the victims. Obi also spoke to Channels Television on the slogan. “They said we said ‘rig and die.’ We didn’t say ‘campaign and die,'” he said. Obi was also reported to have said that the slogan “simply means, do not rig the election. We want a free and fair election. It never meant campaign and die.” He also defended supporters of the Kwankwasiyya movement, who carry sticks to political gatherings. He said they have never used them to harm anyone. However, Keyamo dismissed the explanation, saying Obi’s camp was the one casting itself as the aggrieved party. “This is a classic case of the villain playing the victim,” he said. item.title: Aubameyang escapes injury in car crash ahead of Barcelona clash
item.description: Deportivo La Coruña striker Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang escaped unhurt after his car was involved in a collision with another vehicle while he was driving to the club’s training ground on Thursday. The incident occurred at about 9:23am on the AP-9 motorway in the Piadela area, near the junction with the A6, according to Spanish newspaper Marca. Both vehicles sustained damage, but nobody involved in the accident was injured. Aubameyang continued his journey to Deportivo’s Abegondo training base after the collision and joined his teammates for the scheduled group session. The Gabon international later played down the incident, describing it as a minor scare and expressing relief that everyone involved was safe. “It was just a little scare. These things happen in life. The most important thing is that the other person involved in the accident is fine, and so am I,” he said. The incident comes as Deportivo prepare to host Barcelona at the Riazor Stadium next Sunday, a fixture that will see Aubameyang face his former club. The striker had recently returned to action after recovering from a knee injury that kept him out for a period. He resumed playing at the beginning of November, gradually increasing his involvement in the team. He also experienced ankle discomfort during training last week and underwent medical examinations before recovering sufficiently to travel with the squad for their match against Alavés in Vitoria. Aubameyang had made an impressive start to the season, scoring five goals in his first five official appearances before the knee injury interrupted his run. His availability will be important to Deportivo as they prepare for the Barcelona encounter, with the club relying on his experience and attacking contribution. item.title: Navy dismantles four illegal refineries, recovers 112,525 litres in Rivers
item.description: By Kingsley Omonobi The Nigerian Navy has dismantled four illegal refining sites and uncovered approximately 112,525 litres of suspected stolen crude oil and illegally refined Automotive Gas Oil (AGO) in separate operations in Rivers State. The Director of Information, Navy Captain Abiodun Folorunsho, disclosed this on Thursday, saying the operations exposed repeated attempts by oil thieves to reactivate previously dismantled illegal refining sites. He said the operations were conducted on November 25, 2026, by personnel of Nigerian Navy Ship (NNS) Soroh and Forward Operating Base (FOB) Bonny in Ogbogolo Community, Ahoada West Local Government Area, and George Pepple Community, Bonny Local Government Area. According to him, personnel of NNS Soroh discovered two illegal refining sites at Ogbogolo, containing approximately 15,000 litres of suspected stolen crude oil and 525 litres of suspected illegally refined AGO. The sites also contained three cooking drum ovens, two dugout pits and other equipment used for illegal refining activities. In a separate operation at George Pepple Community, Folorunsho said personnel of FOB Bonny discovered two illegal refining sites comprising 13 dugout pits. He said seven of the pits contained approximately 97,000 litres of suspected stolen crude oil, while four contained water and two were freshly excavated. Folorunsho said all identified facilities and recovered petroleum products were handled in accordance with established procedures. He noted that the operations exposed continued attempts by oil thieves to relocate and reactivate illegal refining activities following previous military operations. “By targeting the facilities used for processing and storing stolen petroleum products, the Nigerian Navy is constraining the operational capacity of criminal operators and disrupting activities that undermine the country’s oil and gas industry,” he said. The Navy spokesman reiterated the service’s commitment to sustaining operations against crude oil theft, illegal bunkering and related criminal activities, particularly to protect critical oil and gas infrastructure. He added that the operations were aimed at safeguarding Nigeria’s energy resources and national economic interests. item.title: 2027: Nwifuru, Umahi, Anyim rally support for Tinubu
item.description: …Umahi targets 1.3m votes, warns against hate speech By Jeff Agbodo, Abakaliki Ebonyi State Governor, Francis Nwifuru; Minister of Works, Senator David Umahi; former Secretary to the Government of the Federation, Anyim Pius Anyim; and former Nigerian Ambassador to Greece, Chief Franklin Ogbuewu, have mobilised support for President Bola Tinubu and other All Progressives Congress (APC) candidates ahead of the 2027 general elections. They declared their support on Thursday during the APC’s state campaign flag-off in Afikpo Local Government Area of Ebonyi State. Addressing supporters at the event, Nwifuru described the APC as a comprehensive political party with candidates for all elective positions in the state and urged residents to vote for Tinubu and other party candidates. The governor commended Tinubu for what he described as massive infrastructure development in Afikpo and urged residents to reciprocate the President’s efforts through their votes in 2027. “We are campaigning for all our candidates, beginning with the President and Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu. “On January 16, 2027, you will be voting for President Bola Ahmed Tinubu. What you will see on the ballot is the symbol of our great party, the broom. That broom represents the unity that has brought us together and sustained the peace we enjoy. “When you thumbprint on the broom, you have voted for President Bola Ahmed Tinubu. On the same day, you will also vote for our senatorial candidate, Professor Anthony Okorie, a distinguished scholar and accomplished academic. “You will equally vote for our own brother, a very calm, resilient, committed and unassuming person, Elumakama Joseph, who is our House of Representatives candidate,” he said. Nwifuru appealed to political leaders and residents of Afikpo to support all APC candidates, arguing that his ability to represent the state effectively would be strengthened by Tinubu’s re-election. “I am not asking you to vote for me alone. I want you to understand that voting for me without voting for President Bola Ahmed Tinubu will not serve our collective interest. “If you vote for me without supporting President Tinubu, I will not have the necessary political leverage to represent you effectively before him,” he said. The governor further urged residents not to take the Federal Government’s projects in the state for granted, claiming that no previous administration since independence had initiated and commissioned infrastructure projects in Ebonyi on the scale of the Tinubu administration. item.title: Lawal reaffirms refusal to negotiate with bandits
item.description: By Idris Salisu, Gusau Zamfara State Governor, Dauda Lawal, has reiterated his administration’s decision not to negotiate with bandits terrorising the state, insisting that efforts would instead focus on reclaiming ungoverned areas and restoring security. Lawal stated this on Thursday at the graduation ceremony of the Zamfara Forest Guards held at Government Secondary School, Gada Biyu, Gusau. More than 1,000 forest guards graduated after undergoing training in weapons handling, physical fitness, combat readiness, civil-military relations, security cooperation, community engagement and the rule of law. The armed forest guard initiative was launched by President Bola Tinubu on May 24, 2025, to train residents to secure forests and other ungoverned areas across the country. At the ceremony, Lawal expressed appreciation to Tinubu and the National Security Adviser for the Federal Government’s support for the initiative. He also commended security agencies, the training coordinator and instructors for their roles in preparing the guards for service. Addressing the graduates and their families, the governor said Zamfara needed to reclaim its vast ungoverned areas, which he said had become hideouts for bandits and other criminal groups. “We must urgently reclaim Zamfara’s vast ungoverned areas, which have become safe havens for bandits, criminals and terrorists. “This will require sustained cooperation between federal and state authorities, a reliable security presence and the restoration of public services. “Our goal is to ensure displaced families can return safely, and communities can farm, trade and rebuild their livelihoods,” he said. The governor said his administration had invested substantially in security agencies over the past three years through the provision of operational equipment, vehicles, surveillance technology and logistical support. He listed the equipment provided to security agencies as more than 30 Armoured Personnel Carriers, 200 operational pick-up vehicles, 20 Toyota Buffalo vehicles and over 1,000 specialised motorcycles. He added that additional vehicles and motorcycles had also been supplied to the Homegrown Community Protection Guards. On surveillance, Lawal said the state had acquired drones, including an 80-metre endurance model capable of covering up to 50 kilometres and operating continuously for eight hours. According to him, the equipment would improve reconnaissance, situational awareness and coordination in difficult terrain. Reaffirming his administration’s position on negotiations with armed groups, the governor said: “I want to make it clear again, we are still firm in our decision never to negotiate with the criminals.” The post Lawal reaffirms refusal to negotiate with bandits appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Fofana apologises over unauthorised interview; Alonso says issue is closed
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso says Wesley Fofana has apologised for giving an unauthorised interview in which he laughed about the penalty miss that knocked the club out of the Carabao Cup against Liverpool. Speaking at his pre-match press conference ahead of Friday’s Premier League game against Nottingham Forest, Alonso said the matter had been addressed and Fofana would be available to play. “We have addressed that with him and for sure it was unfortunate. He has apologised. He knows it wasn’t the right moment. The content wasn’t right,” Alonso said. “We are here to take things seriously and he said it wouldn’t be repeated. We know it’s something we don’t want and they are not going to be repeated.” In the interview with French YouTuber Zack Nani, Fofana said he could “laugh about” the penalty miss. The defender also spoke about having considered retiring from football during one of his spells out with injury at Chelsea. Alonso also urged his players to respond to their 4-1 defeat by Leeds, saying they had failed to meet the standards required to compete. “On Saturday, we missed not just players but many basics to compete in the game. That’s been clear during the week,” he said. “We talked about having those basics to compete, to know what it takes to be ready for each game and we will need that tomorrow.” He said the defeat had been analysed but should not be forgotten. “The idea is that we don’t forget. In the future, we’ll say those standards are not acceptable at this level.” The post Fofana apologises over unauthorised interview; Alonso says issue is closed appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: INEC to test BVAS in 406 Ondo polling units
item.description: By Dayo Johnson, Akure The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) will on Saturday conduct a mock test of its voter accreditation technology in Ondo State ahead of the 2027 general elections. The exercise will take place in 406 polling units across the state’s 18 local government areas between 8:30 a.m. and 2:30 p.m. INEC said the exercise was designed to assess the performance of the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) and identify potential technical challenges ahead of the general elections. In a statement, the Deputy Director and Head of Department, Voter Education and Publicity, Olayinka Ogunseye, said two polling units had been selected from each of the 203 registration areas in the state. The Commission explained that the test would assess how the BVAS performs under different conditions and enable it to address any technical issues identified before the elections. INEC stressed that the exercise was not an election, adding that no voter would cast a ballot for any candidate or political party. It urged residents of the affected polling units, community leaders, political parties, civil society organisations and journalists to cooperate with its officials to ensure a successful exercise. The Commission also cautioned against the spread of rumours and fake news, urging residents to obtain election-related information only through its official communication channels. It said the mock accreditation exercise was part of its early preparations to ensure the smooth deployment of technology and the conduct of credible elections in 2027. item.title: 2027: Atiku tackles Tinubu over rising cost of production, housing
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA — Former Vice President and African Democratic Congress (ADC) presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, has accused President Bola Tinubu’s administration of worsening Nigeria’s cost-of-living crisis through rising energy and production costs. Atiku said expensive and unreliable electricity was forcing manufacturers to spend more on production, pushing up the prices of goods and making homes increasingly unaffordable. In a statement on Thursday by his Director of Strategic Communication, Phrank Shaibu, Atiku cited reports that 11 listed manufacturing companies spent ₦842 billion on energy in the first nine months of 2026, describing the figure as evidence of the burden of unreliable and expensive power. “₦842 billion is the energy bill of only 11 companies in nine months. Cement manufacturers are among the industries hit hardest by the cost of power. That cost does not disappear at the factory gate. It enters the price of every bag of cement and pushes the cost of building a home further beyond the reach of ordinary Nigerians,” he said. Atiku also questioned the Tinubu administration’s claim that it had delivered more than 26,000 housing units, arguing that the figure included unfinished projects and developments initiated under former President Muhammadu Buhari. He noted that 10,328 of the reported units were still under construction and demanded a breakdown of inherited projects, completed houses and those occupied by beneficiaries. “A building site is not a completed home. An inherited project is not proof of fresh delivery. A mortgage approval is not a house key. Publish what Tinubu inherited, what his administration completed, how many families have moved in and what those homes cost,” he said. He also challenged the administration’s claim that its housing programme had generated 525,100 construction jobs, arguing that projected employment opportunities should not be presented as jobs already created. On the wider economic impact, Atiku said the rising cost of energy was forcing manufacturers to increase prices, reduce production, delay expansion or cut jobs, with consumers bearing the consequences. “When factories spend fortunes on electricity, diesel and gas, they raise prices, cut production, postpone expansion or shed jobs. Families then pay more for everything those factories produce. Tinubu’s energy failure is being added to every Nigerian’s bill,” he said. Atiku said his Affordable Life campaign would prioritise reliable electricity for industries and a transparent, targeted subsidy for domestically refined fuel to reduce production costs and ease the burden on consumers. item.title: How I was attacked by gunmen, says Edo NDC victim
item.description: By Ozioruva Aliu BENIN CITY – A member of the Nigerian Democratic Congress (NDC), who sustained gunshot injuries along Airport Road in Benin City while awaiting the arrival of the party’s presidential candidate, Peter Obi, has recounted how he was attacked by gunmen. The victim, Aimionkhale Michael, narrated his experience to journalists at the hospital where he is receiving treatment. Michael, a youth leader from Uromi in Esan North-East Local Government Area and an aide to the NDC House of Representatives candidate for Esan North-East/Esan South-East Federal Constituency, Akhakon Anenih, said he was among party supporters who had gone to the airport to welcome Obi, who was in Edo State for a town hall meeting. He said the supporters remained outside the airport gate because of the heavy security presence. According to him, the scorching sun forced him to seek shelter inside a vehicle while waiting for the presidential candidate’s arrival. “The sun was scorching, so I decided to relax inside the vehicle, with the intention of joining the convoy when they come out,” he said. He alleged that shortly before the shooting, an unidentified man approached him and asked for a fez cap, claiming to be an NDC supporter. Michael said shortly after the man left, a black Toyota Hilux arrived, and its occupants allegedly opened fire indiscriminately. “I told him I didn’t have any cap to give him. Shortly after he left, I saw a black Hilux van. The occupants were shooting and firing everywhere. They shot me at close range on my thigh while I was inside the vehicle. The bullet penetrated my left thigh to the right one,” he said. He said a female police officer and other security operatives rushed him to the hospital after he managed to get out of the vehicle and cried for help. “Immediately, the medical team took me to the theatre, where they commenced treatment. I thank God for sparing my life. I don’t know my attackers or what they are looking for,” he said. He called on the authorities to identify and arrest those responsible for the attack, insisting that political differences should not be allowed to fuel violence. “They should fish out those hoodlums and ensure they are brought to justice. People should understand that elections are not about violence. We are all brothers and sisters, and thugs should not be used to perpetrate violence all in the name of elections,” he added. item.title: FG targets stronger local capacity for energy security
item.description: By Daniel Abia PORT HARCOURT — The Federal Government has expressed its readiness to strengthen local industrial capacity, infrastructure and investment as part of efforts to achieve energy security and accelerate Nigeria’s economic transformation. The Secretary to the Government of the Federation, Senator George Akume, said energy security went beyond the availability of natural resources to include the capacity to produce, process, transport and distribute energy reliably and affordably for the benefit of citizens. Akume spoke in Port Harcourt at the 10th Africa Energy Summit, organised by the Solewant Energy Training Institute, a subsidiary of Solewant Group, with the theme, “Scaling Innovative Industrial Capacity for Africa’s Energy Security.” Represented by his Special Assistant on Technical Matters, Prof. Babatunde Benerd, the SGF said Nigeria’s ambition for economic growth, industrialisation and job creation depended on an energy system capable of meeting the needs of households, businesses and industries. He said the administration of President Bola Tinubu considered reforms in the energy sector, investment and industrial development critical to the country’s economic transformation. “The current administration is pursuing reforms aimed at improving the investment climate, strengthening domestic production and creating conditions for productive activities,” he said. Akume said the implementation of the Petroleum Industry Act had provided a framework for improved governance, clearer institutional responsibilities and increased investment across the oil and gas value chain. He added that the government was promoting domestic gas utilisation, compressed natural gas development, investment in energy infrastructure and reforms in the electricity sector. The SGF stressed that local content should go beyond Nigerian participation in petroleum projects to building competitive enterprises capable of manufacturing products, providing specialised services, creating jobs and competing internationally. Also speaking, the Special Adviser to the President on Energy, Olu Verheijen, represented by Dr Olusegun Amoda, said recent reforms in the sector had helped restore investor confidence and attract fresh investments. Verheijen said the administration had introduced executive orders and policy directives to provide fiscal incentives for investors, reduce contracting timelines and costs, and strengthen local content in the petroleum industry. She said the reforms had contributed to investment decisions worth more than $8 billion in oil and gas projects, adding that improved regulatory stability and security in the Niger Delta had helped create a more favourable investment climate. According to her, oil and gas projects require fabrication, engineering, drilling services, equipment, logistics and maintenance, creating opportunities for local businesses across the value chain. item.title: Ex-BBC commentator Starmer-Smith dies aged 81
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Former England scrum-half and renowned BBC rugby commentator Nigel Starmer-Smith has died aged 81 after a long battle with dementia. His son, Charlie, announced his death in a social media post on Thursday, saying he had “passed away peacefully this morning”. “Dad passed away peacefully this morning after a long battle with dementia,” Charlie wrote. Starmer-Smith was diagnosed with dementia in 2015. In 2021, Charlie described the condition as a major issue in sport and recalled how Covid-19 restrictions meant the family could only see his father through a window. The son also said head injuries were once treated as “like a badge of honour” in rugby and that dementia had affected other members of their family. Starmer-Smith played for Harlequins and the Barbarians and won seven England caps between 1969 and 1971. After retiring in 1976, he moved into broadcasting and journalism. He voiced the BBC’s Rugby Special highlights programme for 15 years and later commentated for ITV at the 2003 Rugby World Cup in Australia, where England won the title. In his tribute, Charlie described his father as “one of life’s great tourists” and remembered him as a player, commentator, writer, charity fundraiser, volunteer and family man. “He was a modest man and he’d hate for people to make a fuss,” Charlie wrote. “He loved to laugh but not as much as he loved to see others laughing.” He urged those who knew his father to think of a happy memory and smile, saying that was how he would remember him. item.title: 2027: Barau mobilises 3,405 Kano traditional rulers for APC
item.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA — Ahead of the 2027 general elections, Deputy President of the Senate, Senator Barau Jibrin, has mobilised 3,405 traditional rulers in Kano State to support President Bola Tinubu, Governor Abba Kabir Yusuf, himself and other candidates of the All Progressives Congress, APC. The meeting, held at the Ali Jita Event Centre in Kano, brought together 3,032 ward heads, 347 village heads and 26 representatives and secretaries of district heads. According to a statement issued on Thursday by Barau’s Special Adviser on Media and Publicity, Ismail Mudashir, the engagement was part of the senator’s ongoing consultations with stakeholders across Kano North Senatorial District. The meeting came barely 72 hours after Barau rallied more than 2,000 Islamic clerics from the 13 local government areas of the district to support Tinubu and other APC candidates in the 2027 elections. Mudashir said the Deputy Senate President had, in recent months, intensified consultations with critical stakeholders across Kano North, urging them to support the President and all APC candidates. Barau commended the traditional rulers for their contributions to grassroots development, describing them as important partners in promoting peace, security and the wellbeing of their communities. He also appreciated their cooperation and prayers, saying traditional institutions remained closest to the people and understood their needs and challenges. On security, the senator acknowledged the challenges confronting some communities in Kano North but expressed optimism that the situation was improving through the collective efforts of security agencies and other stakeholders. He said the deployment of an Army battalion to Dambatta Local Government Area, in addition to existing security formations across the district, would strengthen security and protect lives and property. Highlighting electricity projects across the district, Barau said projects in Bichi, Dawanau Market and Kwanar Kanye in Kabo would cost more than N130 billion. “These projects may take time, but they will definitely turn around the economic fortunes of our senatorial district. I remember when I was in the House of Representatives between 1999 and 2003, similar power projects were attracted to Ogun State by the former President. Today, the state has become an industrial hub. We will get there in Kano North too,” he said. He said the electricity projects, alongside the Federal University of Science and Technology, Kabo; Police Training School; Immigration Training School; and Civil Defence Training School, would stimulate economic activities, create jobs and accelerate development. In the health and education sectors, Barau disclosed plans to upgrade the Bagwai and Kabo hospitals into major referral and teaching hospitals, with the Kabo facility expected to serve as a teaching hospital for the Federal University of Science and Technology. item.title: Mock Accreditation: INEC Faces Crucial Test As 100 Million Voters Await 2027 Elections
item.description: With exactly 50 days before Nigerians return to the ballot, the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) is preparing for a nationwide test that could offer an important indication of whether the country is ready for another fiercely contested general election. On Saturday, November 28, the electoral umpire will deploy its Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) and electronic results upload technology across 17,676 selected polling units in a mock exercise designed to identify operational weaknesses, test equipment reliability and strengthen public confidence ahead of the 2027 elections. The exercise, scheduled for 8:30 a.m. to 2:30 p.m., will cover two polling units in each of the country’s 8,838 registration areas, giving INEC an opportunity to assess the performance of its electoral technology across different locations before the presidential and National Assembly elections on January 16, 2027, and the governorship and State Houses of Assembly elections on February 6. #OsunDecides2026: Election Officers Take Delivery Of Materials, Mobilise To Polling Units during the Osun State governorship election on August 15, 2026. It comes against the backdrop of lingering controversies surrounding the 2023 general elections, particularly the failure to upload presidential election results to the INEC Result Viewing Portal (IReV) in real time, technical difficulties associated with BVAS and allegations of electoral irregularities. Chairman of INEC, Joash Amupitan, described the mock exercise as an important part of preparations for the forthcoming elections, while urging Nigerians to participate. The commission’s Director of Voter Education and Publicity, Victoria Meci, explained that the exercise would allow INEC to establish the effectiveness and reliability of its equipment before election day. “We don’t want to wait till the elections before we test the ruggedness, readiness and functionality of the system,” she said during an appearance on Channels Television’s Sunrise Daily . According to her, the commission has reduced the accreditation threshold to 850 voters per BVAS device, with additional machines to be provided at polling units with larger voter populations. The exercise will also test the electronic upload of results to IReV, although Meci acknowledged that successful transmission would depend on network availability. 100 Million Voters, 176,846 Polling Units The scale of the preparations reflects the size of Nigeria’s electorate. INEC says it is now managing a verified national register of more than 100 million voters after removing over 1.6 million invalid, duplicated, and deceased records from the previous register of approximately 103 million. Amupitan disclosed on Wednesday, during a meeting with resident electoral commissioners from the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory, that the clean-up followed the application of an Automated Biometric Identification System and a statutory claims-and-objections audit. item.title: Driver Arrested Over Crash, Inferno That Killed 31 In Egypt
item.description: Egyptian prosecutors announced on Thursday the arrest of a man accused of causing a massive fire that erupted when a fuel tanker overturned on a packed highway in Cairo, killing 31 people. The prosecution said the man had “admitted” to speeding when his car collided with the tanker, “causing the steering wheel to slip from his hands and his car to veer off course”. When the car hit the truck, one of its tyres exploded, causing it to overturn, the prosecution said. The fire erupted as a result of a petrol leak, it added. This video grab taken from UGC images posted on social media on November 25, 2026, shows flames engulfing the area during a fire in the Al-Waraq neighbourhood of Imbaba district, Giza Governorate. Photo by – / VARIOUS SOURCES / AFP Footage from the scene showed a huge fireball and thick black smoke rising above the densely populated capital’s Al-Waraq neighbourhood as motorists on the ring road sounded their horns and struggled to get away.The prosecution said an investigation is underway to determine the driver’s criminal liability.The health ministry put the final toll at 31 dead and 21 wounded.More than 20 million people live in Greater Cairo, a sprawling and dense metropolis. With its informal residential areas and often dilapidated infrastructure, Egypt has suffered several deadly fires in recent years. Car crashes are common and often blamed on reckless driving, poor maintenance, and uneven law enforcement, with traffic laws also being widely flouted. Last year, nearly 6,000 people died in road accidents across the country, according to Egypt’s state statistics agency. Flames And Smoke In 2018, the government issued a decision banning heavy transport vehicles from accessing the ring road around Greater Cairo from 6:00 am to midnight. Emergency services personnel and bystanders gather beside the wreckage of a tanker truck following a fire in the Al-Waraq neighbourhood of Imbaba district, Giza Governorate, on November 25, 2026. Photo by MAHMOUD EL-KHAWAS / AFP Wednesday’s disaster occurred at around 7:00 pm — at a time when the road was packed with pedestrians, buses and cars.Traffic had returned to normal in the early hours of Thursday after rescue operations ended and the wreckage of the truck and burned-out cars was cleared.”We were driving on the flyover above the ring road and saw flames rising to a height I can’t even describe,” said Wagih Ragheb, a witness to the disaster.”Then the explosions started… We got out of the car and went down to the ring road and found a catastrophic situation: buses and cars completely charred, and many dead.” Footage posted online by passersby showed people pulling others out of their cars in the inferno that erupted after the truck overturned. “We have a problem with our roads. These accidents happen very often, and no one knows how to solve this,” said Abdel Rahman Ahmed, who was at a Cairo hospital to donate blood for the wounded. item.description: The clash between Kambari vigilantes and Fulani herders in Borgu Local Government Area of Niger State resulted in the death of 74 persons. The state’s governor, Mohammed Umaru Bago, disclosed this during a visit to the Emir of Borgu, Alhaji Halilu Sani Dantoro, at his palace in New Bussa, the LGA’s headquarters. Terrorists had, last Saturday, attacked Lumman-Ba’are community in Borgu LGA, killing the village head, Mallam Bawa Muhammad, his wife and three of his children. They also set his palace ablaze. Niger State Governor, Mohammed Umaru Bago, has ordered a thorough investigation into the clashes.‎ ‎The governor commiserated with the traditional ruler and people of the kingdom over the tragic incident. ‎Bago said the investigation was aimed at identifying those responsible for the violence and uncovering the remote and immediate causes of the recurring communal conflicts, with a view to preventing future occurrences. ‎He called on residents of the affected communities to embrace peaceful coexistence, tolerance and mutual understanding, stressing that no meaningful development could take place in an atmosphere of violence and hostility. ‎The governor expressed sympathy with the families of the victims and announced a donation of ₦2 million to each of the 74 affected families, amounting to ₦148 million, alongside the provision of foodstuffs and building materials to support those whose houses were destroyed during the clashes. ‎He commended the Borgu Emirate Council for its continued efforts towards maintaining peace and unity among the people, while urging Nigerians to learn to live together irrespective of their differences. ‎In his response, the Emir of Borgu, Muhammad Haliru -Dantoro Kitoro IV, appreciated the governor for the condolence visit and the timely deployment of security personnel to the area. ‎The traditional ruler acknowledged the state government’s efforts in deploying joint tactical security teams to tackle security challenges, including insurgency, in the area. He, however, expressed sadness that some individuals had chosen to resort to violence despite ongoing efforts by the government and security agencies to restore lasting peace. ‎The Emir also commended security agencies for their swift response, which he said helped to contain the situation and restore normalcy to the affected communities. ‎In his remarks, the Minister of State for Agriculture, Senator Sabi Abdullahi, commended President Bola Ahmed Tinubu for his efforts towards addressing security challenges across the country, noting that the restructuring of the nation’s security architecture was yielding positive results. ‎He also praised Governor Bago for his commitment to tackling insecurity in parts of Niger State and acknowledged the contributions of security agencies in containing threats to lives and property. ‎The governor was accompanied on the visit by the Minister of State for Agriculture, Senator Sabi Abdullahi; Member representing Borgu/Agwara Federal Cons
